title: Justify coefficient extraction in symbols q^{k^alpha} (independence)

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Justification of coefficient extraction (rigor gap shared by both parts).**

The problem fixes a complex number $\alpha$ and asks to interpret the LHS "as formal power series in $x$ with coefficients in the ring of formal expressions in $q$ and $q^{k^\alpha}$ for positive integers $k$."

A solver must:
1. State precisely the coefficient ring, treating the symbols $Q_k:=q^{k^\alpha}$ ($k\ge1$) as **algebraically independent indeterminates** over $\mathbb Z$ (or $\mathbb Q$).
2. Show that for each fixed $n$, only finitely many $Q_k$ (namely $k\le n$) appear on either side, so the formal manipulations $\tfrac{x^k}{1-x^k}=\sum_{m\ge1}x^{km}$ and the product with $P(x)$ are legitimate.
3. Conclude that equality of the two formal power series is **equivalent** to equality of the coefficient of every monomial $Q_k\,x^n$.

This step is what makes both the proof of (ii) and the disproof of (i) airtight: it rules out the worry that accidental relations among the genuine numbers $q^{k^\alpha}$ could create cancellations. Without it, the single-point disproof of (i) is not rigorous.

Also address $\alpha$-independence: $M_v(n),N_v(n),R_v(n)$ are $\alpha$-free integers, so the conclusions hold for every $\alpha$.
